A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IFPRUNING work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and additions in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, scaling experiments, parameter-overlap analyses and comparisons of input-specific versus task-specific pruning.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds inference-latency measurements, a continued-pretraining ablation and a MoE latency comparison.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same prompt-conditioned FFN pruning, SoftTopK masks and joint continued-pretraining/SFT procedure. Newly specified predictor dimensions and parameter-caching details document implementation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The training mixture and evaluated datasets, languages and tasks are retained, including translation and parameter-overlap domains. The new ablation reuses existing benchmarks; latency simulations introduce model and workload configurations rather than new data domains or language tasks.

E2.justification: The accuracy comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B as an actually evaluated latency comparator. Newly discussed pruning methods in related work are not added accuracy baselines.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a substantial latency-evaluation protocol: batch size 1, four responses per query, 4,000 input tokens, 100 generated tokens, and separate selection, loading, prefill, TTFT and decoding measurements. Appendix A.5 specifies an RTX A6000 GPU. A separate ablation introduces SFT-only versus continued-pretraining-plus-SFT controls; existing accuracy settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4/Table 5 adds a focused ablation testing continued pre-training before SFT for 6B-to-3B pruning across six existing benchmarks. Earlier scaling, domain-overlap and task-specific pruning analyses remain. Appendix A.3 expands documentation of the existing overlap analysis rather than adding another experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed comparisons, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The four responses per latency query specify the workload, not an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. V3 adds substantial new results: Table 3 reports internal-model TTFT of 0.846 seconds for DENSE-9B versus 0.471 for IFPRUNING; Table 5 reports GSM8K scores of 50.9 for SFT-only versus 61.3 with continued pre-training. Appendix A.5 adds MoE timings. These are new comparisons, not revised main-table accuracy scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), sparsity constraints and the mathematical pruning/training formulation remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. Added descriptions of overlap averaging and baseline distillation provide implementation detail rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and central dynamic-pruning accuracy claims remain unchanged. The introduction adds explicit claims of near-static-pruning runtime, up to 57% lower TTFT, 41% lower generation time and negligible dynamic-pruning overhead, extending the paper's practical efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V3 interprets GPU timing simulations as evidence of practical edge-device suitability and attributes MoE's slower small-batch decoding to expert-weight loading. Existing limitations concerning heterogeneous server batches and end-to-end training are largely retained within the conclusion, rather than removed.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility information: the predictor's 128-unit MLP bottleneck, a 12B distillation teacher, combined next-token/KL loss with truncated teacher distributions, and 128-input sampling and pairwise averaging for the existing overlap analysis. It also documents parameter caching and latency hardware/workloads. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Related work adds a SliceGPT discussion and references covering additional pruning, activation and MoE research, including LACO, ZipLM, GLaM and ST-MoE. The existing positioning against static pruning and token-level conditional computation remains, with greater emphasis on on-device use.

P1.justification: Most core prose and section order remain intact. V3 expands the task-specific pruning explanation, clarifies terminology, incorporates limitations into the conclusion, adds acknowledgements and reorganizes the appendix. These are localized editorial and structural changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V3 adopts an ICML layout with running headers, revised caption placement and a full-width appendix. Figure 1 is substantially redesigned and adds a TTFT panel; Figure 3 receives revised labels and placement. New latency, ablation and MoE displays accompany the retained and renumbered tables.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful tests of inference efficiency and continued pre-training, plus missing implementation details. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 3 implies at most about 44% TTFT reduction, not the claimed 57%, and Appendix A.5 describes LLaMA pruning while repeating the internal-model timings. The main accuracy evidence remains intact, but the new efficiency conclusions need tighter support.
